units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 4:1:9">Y. Meg. IV, 74ᵈ</cite> bot. <he>יכיל … ק׳ מן פומי</he> I can write the entire Scriptures from memory; <he>יכיל … ק׳ בתרין מניי</he> I can write the whole Bible at a cost of two Manehs; <he>וכתב כל ק׳ על וכ׳</he> and wrote the whole Bible on their hides.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 2:4:9">Y. Ber. II, 4ᵈ</cite> bot. <he>כמא דאישתעי ק׳ כך וכ׳</he> the phraseology of the Bible must be adopted in Talmudic diction; Y. Snh. VIII, 25ᶜ.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Peah 1:1:37">Y. Peah I, 15ᵈ</cite> bot. <he>שמע … מן הדין ק׳</he> understood (derived) all this from the following verse.

<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 22:9">Lev. R. s. 22</cite> <he>אי מן הדא ק׳ לית וכ׳</he> if you mean to prove from this verse, you cannot derive from it anything; a. v. fr.—Pl. <he>קָרַיָּיא</he> (v. <cite ref="S01876"><he>קְרָא</he> II</cite>), <cite ref="S02056"><he>קַרְיָין</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 1:3:2">Y. Ber. I, 3ᵇ</cite> <he>הא רב״ה מקיימין תרין ק׳</he> (not <he>מקימון</he>) with this interpretation of Beth Hillel the two texts are harmonized.

<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 3:14:1">Koh. R. to III, 14</cite> <he>היאך מרי … אילין ק׳ וכ׳</he> how do you explain these verses?, and he delivered them to him; <he>ואילין ק׳ מקרי ליה</he> (not <he>מקרתן</he>) and these are the verses he interpreted to him. Lev. R. l. c. <he>אית ליה ק׳ סגיין</he> he has many Biblical verses to prove his opinion; a. fr.
